tasks.short: Read incoming CVs in Recruitee against the vacancy and hiring manager's order, mark who fits.

today.trigger: New applications land in Recruitee, or a manager raises a new vacancy or headcount request.
steps: Open the vacancy and the manager's intake notes
Read each CV and motivation letter in Recruitee
Check hard requirements: forklift, VCA, driving licence code C/CE, shift availability, Dutch level
Tag or move the candidate to a stage, note why
Batch the shortlist to the manager by email or Teams
drudgery: Reading many near-identical CVs for warehouse roles
Hunting for certificate numbers and licence codes in PDFs
today.time_sinks: Peak season volume for order pickers and drivers, and AI-written applications that all look alike.

lenses.faster: An LLM step extracts certificates, licence codes, shift availability and language level into Recruitee fields and lists which requirements each CV meets or misses, with the source line quoted.
lenses.autonomous: Extraction and the requirement checklist run on each new application; nothing is rejected without the recruiter opening it.
lenses.ambitious: Every applicant gets read the same day, including the long tail for office roles that today waits a week.
lenses.joy: No more scanning PDFs for a VCA number; the recruiter spends the time on the borderline candidates.
lenses.options: Show the candidate against two or three other open vacancies at other sites (Tilburg picker who could fit Venlo).
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the requirement lists per role family and audits a sample of the checklists each week.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate and licence verification before contract
L&D Specialist: spotting which hires will need forklift or VCA training in Studytube

tasks.human_edge: Judging potential behind a thin CV, career switchers, and what the manager really needs beyond the order.
tasks.pattern_why: Filtering applications is high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027 and GDPR Art. 22 bars rejection on a score alone, so the AI extracts and explains while the recruiter decides.

steps: Parse CV and letter into structured fields (certificates, licences, shifts, languages)
Compare against the role's written must-haves and nice-to-haves
Write a requirement checklist with quoted evidence to a Recruitee note
Recruiter reviews, moves stage, records reason
Log input, output and recruiter decision
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter opens every application before any stage move; no automatic rejection.
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee notes plus a decision log kept at least six months

evidence.claim: 67% of US hiring leaders use AI for CV screening; 26% fear they no longer see some candidates
AFAS Profit 8 builds a profile from an application and calculates a match score against open vacancies
Match scores built from data beyond the application are under legal attack (Kistler v. Eightfold)

risks: Works council consent needed first (WOR art. 27(1)(k)/(l)); without it the arrangement can be voided
Rubber-stamping turns review into no meaningful human intervention under Art. 22
Extraction errors on scanned or non-Dutch CVs
Proxy bias via postcode, gaps or name
research_questions: How accurate is extraction of licence codes and VCA/forklift certificates on 200 real Noordhaven CVs?
Will the OR consent to an extraction-plus-checklist tool, and under what conditions?
Does the AFAS Profit 8 match score expose its reasons, or is it a black box we should not use?
How much recruiter time per application goes to reading versus deciding today?

tasks.short: Explain the job to candidates: tasks, CAO pay scale, shifts, allowances, travel, site conditions.

today.trigger: Candidate calls, emails or asks during a screening call or interview.
steps: Look up the CAO scale and shift allowances for the role
Answer by phone or email, often the same questions repeatedly
Explain shift patterns, cold store or night work, site access
Send the offer details or brochure from SharePoint
drudgery: Repeating the same pay, shift and travel answers
Looking up which CAO and scale applies to which site
today.time_sinks: Phone tag with shift-working candidates and inconsistent answers between the two recruiters.

lenses.faster: A per-role fact pack (pay scale, allowances, shifts, site, travel allowance) is generated from the CAO tables and vacancy, and email answers are drafted from it.
lenses.autonomous: A candidate-facing assistant on the careers page and WhatsApp answers factual questions from the approved pack, says it is AI and from Noordhaven at the first turn, and hands off anything personal.
lenses.ambitious: Every candidate gets an honest realistic job preview (night shifts, cold store, lifting) before the interview, which should lift 90-day retention.
lenses.joy: Recruiters stop reciting allowance tables and keep the conversations about fit and doubts.
lenses.options: Draft three versions of the job pack: short WhatsApp, full email, and plain-language for candidates with limited Dutch.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter maintains the source fact packs and reviews the assistant's handoffs and wrong answers weekly.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: keeping the CAO pay tables current

tasks.human_edge: Handling doubts, negotiating, and being honest about hard parts of the job in a way that builds trust.
tasks.pattern_why: Factual questions answered from a fixed, approved pack are checkable; the model only retrieves and phrases.

in_practice.trigger: Candidate question by email, careers page chat or WhatsApp.
steps: Classify question: factual, personal or negotiation
Answer factual ones from the approved role pack with AI notice
Route personal or negotiation questions to the recruiter with a draft
Recruiter approves drafts; assistant logs what it answered
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves any non-factual answer and every pay-related offer detail.
data_needed: CAO pay scales and allowances per site

evidence.claim: A candidate-facing chatbot must disclose it is AI at the first turn; fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of turnover
evidence.source: Warden AI on AI Act Art. 50 [S9]

evidence.claim: Retrieval-based assistants answer FAQ reliably when restricted to an approved source

risks: Wrong pay or allowance stated creates an expectation or dispute
Stale fact pack after a CAO update
Candidates with limited Dutch misread automated answers
research_questions: What share of candidate questions are purely factual in a two-week sample?
Who owns updating the fact packs when the CAO changes?
Do realistic job previews reduce early leavers at Noordhaven's sites?

tasks.short: Pick the candidates to put forward to the manager and give a hiring advice after interviews.

steps: Compare shortlisted candidates on notes and interview feedback
Call manager to discuss
Write a short recommendation
Agree who gets an offer
drudgery: Writing the same comparison table by hand
today.time_sinks: Chasing managers for scorecards and aligning two or three interviewers.

lenses.faster: A side-by-side brief pulls structured interview scores and recruiter notes per criterion, flagging missing feedback.
lenses.autonomous: The brief assembles when the last scorecard is in; reminders go to managers who have not filled theirs.
lenses.ambitious: Each recommendation is later checked against day-90 outcome from AFAS, so the team learns which signals predict who stays.
lenses.joy: No more copying notes into Word; the recruiter argues the case with the manager.
lenses.options: Show two or three ranked options with the trade-offs, not a single pick.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter designs the scorecards and reviews whether recommendations held up at day 90.
reach: HR Business Partner: advising managers on team composition

tasks.human_edge: Weighing fit, motivation and the manager's real constraints; standing behind the advice.
tasks.pattern_why: Evaluating candidates is high-risk use and decision-making must stay with people; AI prepares, the recruiter recommends.

in_practice.trigger: All scorecards for a candidate set submitted in Recruitee.
steps: Assemble criteria-by-candidate comparison from scorecards
Flag gaps and contradictory ratings
Recruiter writes the recommendation
Manager decides; outcome logged
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter writes and owns the recommendation; manager decides.

evidence.claim: AI interview summaries become the record and can carry errors and unlawful questions
No rejection based solely on a score; human review must be real

risks: Managers read the brief instead of their own notes
Summaries drop context
Outcome loop needs AFAS-Recruitee data linking under AVG purpose limits
research_questions: Do Noordhaven managers fill structured scorecards today, and how often?
Can AFAS day-90 status be linked to Recruitee candidates lawfully?
Does the comparison brief change any recommendations in a pilot of 20 vacancies?

tasks.short: Let candidates know where they stand: received, invited, on hold, rejected, offer.

today.trigger: Stage change in Recruitee or a candidate asking.
steps: Pick a template in Recruitee or write an email
Personalise rejections after interviews
Call candidates who interviewed
Answer 'any news?' mails
drudgery: Answering chasers because updates were late
today.time_sinks: Candidates left waiting while managers decide, which generates follow-up mail and drop-outs.

lenses.faster: Stage changes trigger templated messages; post-interview rejections get an LLM-drafted personal note from the scorecard for recruiter approval.
lenses.autonomous: A rule sends a 'still in progress' update when a candidate sits in a stage longer than the set days, and flags the stuck stage to the manager.
lenses.ambitious: Every candidate hears within 48 hours of each step, which protects acceptance rate in a tight labour market.
lenses.joy: No more chasers; phone calls are kept for finalists.
lenses.options: Draft rejection notes in Dutch, English and Polish for agency-sourced candidates.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter sets the stage SLAs and templates and watches the stuck-stage report.
reach: HR Business Partner: nudging managers on overdue decisions

tasks.human_edge: Calling finalists who are rejected and delivering offers personally.
tasks.pattern_why: Stage-triggered messages and SLA timers are rule-based; only personalised rejections need a draft step.

in_practice.trigger: Recruitee stage change or stage age over threshold.
steps: Send template for the new stage
Start SLA timer per stage
Send holding update and alert manager when overdue
Draft personal rejection after interview for approval
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves post-interview rejections; first-stage templates send automatically.

evidence.claim: Uniper's hiring agent flagged overdue tasks and coordinated candidate emails; time to contract fell 27 days
Recruiter-reviewed emails need no AI label

risks: A rejection template fires on a mis-click stage move
Impersonal tone hurts employer brand among local warehouse workers
research_questions: How long do candidates sit in each Recruitee stage today?
Does Recruitee's automation support SLA timers natively or do we need a workflow tool?
How many chaser emails per week do recruiters handle?

tasks.short: Find candidates: post ads, search LinkedIn and the CV database, referrals, job fairs, agencies.

today.trigger: Vacancy opened or few applicants after a week.
steps: Write and post the vacancy on job boards
Search LinkedIn and Recruitee talent pool
Message possible candidates
Ask agencies for flex workers or candidates
Organise or attend local job fairs
drudgery: Writing outreach messages one by one
today.time_sinks: Hard-to-fill roles: CE drivers, maintenance technicians, planners.

lenses.faster: Ads per board and personalised outreach are drafted in batches; the talent pool is searched against the role's must-haves.
lenses.autonomous: An agent proposes a weekly list of past applicants and silver medallists for new vacancies with drafted messages; the recruiter approves each send.
lenses.ambitious: A proper flex-to-permanent pipeline: good flex workers from the agency portals are invited to apply for permanent roles.
lenses.joy: Less copy-paste, more time on referrals and talking to people at job fairs.
lenses.options: Five ad variants per role tested across boards and sites.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter runs the sourcing channel mix and judges which channel produces hires still there at day 90.
reach: Coordinating agency orders with the three staffing agencies

tasks.human_edge: Networking, referral conversations, persuading passive candidates, agency relationships.
tasks.pattern_why: Several tools and steps, but every outreach goes to a real person so each send is approved.

in_practice.trigger: Vacancy open with fewer than target applicants after N days.
steps: Search talent pool and past applicants within retention consent
Draft ad variants and outreach messages
Recruiter approves each message
Track response and channel to hire
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves every outreach message before it is sent.

evidence.claim: Workday's TA agent drafts outreach; outreach still requires recruiter approval
57% of hiring leaders use AI for job descriptions
Targeting job ads becomes high-risk from 2 December 2027

risks: Contacting past applicants beyond the AVG retention period (usually four weeks, one year with consent)
Using agency data on flex workers without a clear legal basis
Ad targeting excluding groups
research_questions: How many past applicants in Recruitee have valid one-year consent?
Do the agency contracts allow approaching flex workers for permanent jobs?
Which channel produced hires still employed at day 90 last year?

tasks.short: Check that our selection criteria and tests are fair, relevant and legal; propose changes.

today.trigger: Yearly review, a complaint, or a manager asking for new criteria.
steps: Pull pipeline data from Recruitee into Excel
Look at pass rates per stage
Review job requirements with managers
Write recommendations
today.time_sinks: Data cleaning and the lack of outcome data linked to selection.

lenses.faster: A standing Power BI report shows pass rates per stage, role and source; an LLM reviews criteria text for unnecessary or exclusionary requirements.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly the report flags stages with sharp drop-offs or criteria that no hire actually needed.
lenses.ambitious: Selection criteria are validated against day-90 retention for the first time, and the file is ready for AI Act high-risk duties in December 2027.
lenses.joy: No more Excel exports; the work becomes the conversation with managers about what matters.
lenses.options: Scenario: what happens to the shortlist if a requirement is dropped or loosened.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter becomes the competent overseer for any AI in selection, owning logs and fairness checks.
reach: People Analytics: funnel and adverse impact analysis
HR Director: AI governance and works council reporting

tasks.human_edge: Judging what is job-relevant and defending changes to managers and the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Analysis can be automated but the judgement about fairness and relevance is a human responsibility.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly report or new AI tool proposed.
steps: Refresh stage pass-rate report
LLM reviews criteria text and flags issues
Recruiter reviews with People Analytics
Recommendations to HR Director and OR
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter and HR Director approve any criteria change.

evidence.claim: From 2 December 2027 deployers need a competent overseer, six months of logs and must inform workers' representatives
The AP finds recruitment AI weak on explainability

risks: No lawful data on protected characteristics, so fairness checks rely on proxies
Small numbers per role make statistics weak
research_questions: Which fairness checks are possible with data Noordhaven may lawfully hold?
Is the sample per role big enough to see anything?
What will the OR want to see before consenting to AI in selection?

tasks.short: Plan how we will fill expected roles: channels, timing, seasonal peaks, flex versus permanent.

today.trigger: Budget round, peak season planning, or a new client contract.
steps: Collect headcount plans from managers
Look at turnover and open vacancies
Agree channel and agency mix
Present plan to HR Director
today.time_sinks: Waiting for manager input and reconciling flex numbers with agency invoices.

lenses.faster: A model combines AFAS headcount, attrition, Recruitee time-to-hire and agency hours into a hiring forecast per site.
lenses.autonomous: Forecast refreshes monthly and flags roles at risk of missing their fill date.
lenses.ambitious: Scenario plans for each new client contract within a day, including how many flex workers to convert.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet merging, more strategy with managers.
lenses.options: Three scenarios: base, peak, new contract, with costs per scenario.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the planning model and its assumptions.

tasks.human_edge: Reading the business, negotiating budget and agency terms.
tasks.pattern_why: Data assembly is automatable; strategy and trade-offs stay with people.

steps: Pull AFAS, Recruitee and agency data
Build forecast and scenarios
Recruiter adjusts and writes the plan
HR Director approves
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director approves the plan and budget.

evidence.claim: Workday's agent flags roles at risk of missing their fill date
Pipeline monitoring needs process context to be useful

risks: Forecasts treated as certain
Agency data inconsistent across three portals
research_questions: Can agency hours be extracted reliably from all three portals?
How accurate would last year's forecast have been?
What lead time does a new client contract give?

tasks.short: Build and run applicant tests: work samples, Excel or planning tests, practical checks for warehouse roles.

today.trigger: New role type or manager asks for a test.
steps: Agree content with the manager
Build the test
Schedule and run it
Score and discuss results

lenses.faster: Draft test items and scoring rubrics per role from the job profile; auto-score knowledge items.
lenses.autonomous: Knowledge tests score automatically; certificate checks pull from Studytube.
lenses.ambitious: Valid, job-related work samples for every role family, checked against day-90 performance.
lenses.joy: Less item writing, more time on test design.
lenses.options: Several test variants to avoid leaks.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter designs test standards and reviews validity.
reach: L&D Specialist: aligning tests with training needs

tasks.human_edge: Observing practical tests and judging job-relevance.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting and scoring can be supported; test validity and use stay human, and emotion inference is banned.

steps: Draft items and rubric
Manager and recruiter review
Run test, auto-score knowledge items
Review results
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves every test and reviews scores before decisions.

evidence.claim: Workday's TA team generated interview questions for 800+ skills; no evidence of better hires
Emotion inference in hiring is banned

risks: Tests not validated
Language bias against non-native candidates
research_questions: Which roles use tests today?
Do test scores predict day-90 retention?
Does OR consent cover tests?

role.altitude: From moving candidates through stages to owning the hiring system: stage SLAs, templates, criteria, AI oversight and the day-90 feedback loop.
reach: HR Administrator: pre-start and certificate checks
People Analytics: funnel and fairness reporting
Flex worker coordination with staffing agencies
role.ceiling_note: Interviews, persuasion, manager relations and legal gates (OR consent, AI Act from Dec 2027, GDPR Art. 22) limit automation; about 30 to 40% of 3,200 hours could be freed.
role.ambitious_version: Every candidate hears within 48 hours, criteria are tested against who stays at day 90, and flex workers become a real permanent hiring pipeline.
